The meal that comes second in the day, after breakfast, is lunch.

Regarding the thematic structure in the provided text, the author’s motive appears to be the exploration of the parallel between botanical decay and human emotional isolation. By using the wilting sunflower as a central metaphor, the author structurally links the natural cycle of life and decay to the protagonist's internal state. This thematic connection serves to urge readers to reflect on how neglect—whether directed at a plant or a personal relationship—leads to inevitable deterioration, thereby reinforcing the theme of human connection through the lens of natural consequences.
